steps.name: Diane
steps.text: Vina... I don't like this story.

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: The King who found no peace in his eternal rest upon the throne, and the hero who laid down her crown…

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: The story's over, but has anything really changed?

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: You and King Alistair both wanted to make Victoria better… but in the end…
Diane takes a hard swig from the bottle.

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: Cough—cough!
The burning liquor stings, coaxing more tears from her already swollen eyes.

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: If the King couldn't do it, then what hope do we have?

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: How can we possibly change anything?

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: But the story's not over yet, Diane.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: I had also believed it would all end when the king found peace... but then someone unexpected appeared.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Should I even ask what brings you here?
A white figure emerges from the shadows behind the throne.

a.text: 'Faint glimpses of that fairy can be seen in so many of Victoria's legends…'
'Power, intrigue, destiny, dreams coming true—throughout the centuries-old tales, she seems to possess different powers. Yet no one can say for certain which one is truly her.'

steps.text: 'Vina, who did you see?'
Vina, you've far exceeded my expectations. You've shown me new possibilities.

steps.name: Unicorn
steps.text: Put down your hammer. I am not your enemy.

steps.name: Unicorn
steps.text: We fought side by side once, didn't we?

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Who are you, Unicorn?

steps.name: Unicorn
steps.text: A tailor's daughter, a leader of the Self-Salvation Corps, a witness to Victoria...

steps.name: Unicorn
steps.text: Of course, many old men, even as they faced death, insisted on calling me 'the Nation's Sentinel' in their history books. Wishful thinking, I suppose.

steps.name: Unicorn
steps.text: Over the hundreds of years I've remained in Victoria, I've assumed, and later erased, countless identities, but at present, I am Clovisia.

steps.name: Unicorn
steps.text: In short, I am your friend, one sincerely pleased by all you've achieved. Does this answer satisfy you, Vina?

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Another one of the 'long-lived'? You deceived every ally in the Self-Salvation Corps, as well as all of Rhodes Island.

steps.name: Unicorn
steps.text: Deceived? I've never deceived anyone. Everyone has their desires; I merely fulfill them.

steps.name: Unicorn
steps.text: Ordinary people tormented by Sarkaz bloodshed wanted to survive, so I led the Self-Salvation Corps to find a way out.

steps.name: Unicorn
steps.text: Ancient families, mired in power struggles, feared annihilation in the Empire's whirlpool, so I eliminated every threat to the continuation of the ducal lineage.

steps.name: Unicorn
steps.text: Frederick III hoped Victoria wouldn't fall into chaos beneath the Red Dragon's shadow—I could grant that wish, too.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: So now you've come to me?

steps.name: Unicorn
steps.text: Alexandrina, daughter of Alistair, why would you think I'm only just noticing you now?

steps.name: Unicorn
steps.text: Vina, history is like a sailing ship, and you all are the ones who steer its course.

steps.name: Unicorn
steps.text: Since you wish to change Victoria, I can help you. What role would you assume to realize your ideals?

steps.name: Unicorn
steps.text: You could be a king, a speaker, or even the sole leader of The Exemplars—any of these titles are yours to choose.
'Vina, I must say, yours isn't a new story. I've read far too many like it in old shops...'
'In the end, the hero always accepts the fairy's gift. So, in the end, you chose the role of speaker?'

a.text: 'For hundreds of years, the Unicorn has chosen the heroes, and the heroes have merely chosen their boons.'
'Yes, why did I have to choose her?'

steps.name: Unicorn
steps.text: Why are you laughing, Vina?

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Do you hear that sound outside?

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: They're cheering for victory, and for Victoria.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Many of them do not have grand ambitions. They don't think of protecting anyone. Some of them would not even share a piece of bread with a starving man.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Yet they are still willing to risk their lives for even the smallest sliver of hope. They are my 'Victoria'.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: I like those fools, and I'm willing to look out for them.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: And you, Clovisia, have no right to make me choose something I've been doing all along.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: You'd best leave, unless you don't mind it getting awkward.
Siege!

steps.name: Unicorn
steps.text: You're a fool too, Alexandrina—just like your father.

steps.name: Unicorn
steps.text: Send them a message for me. Tell them the tailor's daughter is dead.

steps.name: Unicorn
steps.text: I have fulfilled their wishes.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Siege! I got the Crawler in here to back you up!

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: We've been waiting outside for you forever. We were afraid something happened to you.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: It's been taken care of. Thank you, Feist.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Come on then. Aren't they still all waiting for us? This battle must end now.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: That's the end of the story, Diane.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Diane?
The condemned soldier has finished the last drop of alcohol and is sound asleep.
Diane wanted to drink herself into a stupor. Vina has finished telling her story, but Diane cannot bring herself to face her own ending.
She wanted to drink herself into a dream, a dream in which even death could not catch up to her. She gets her wish.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: *sigh*

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: I'm sorry, Diane. I am not worthy of being a monarch. I'm not even sure I'm qualified to serve as speaker.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Besides, this war has changed many things. Old beliefs have been shattered, and we are striving to rebuild our lives amidst the imminent threat of destruction.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: I believe that soon, a great transformation will begin in Londinium and sweep across all of Victoria...

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: I don't know what tomorrow will bring, but I am certain of one thing: now that we've found the courage to face adversity, why should we ever return to the past?

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Victoria no longer needs a monarch, Diane.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Sweet dreams.
On the eve of her march to the gallows, the drunken soldier sleeps the most peaceful sleep of her life.

She dreams of the king's coronation. She dreams of the factory in her hometown, the whistle blowing to signal the end of the workday, as the workers shake off their hats and step out through the factory gates…
Then she soars into the sky and sees Londinium gliding across the mist-covered, verdant earth.
She dreams of Victoria. She is singing her song.

a.text: May the vast lands they keep owre kynge ♪
His people, and alle his well-wyllynge ♪
And give them grace wythoute endying ♪
Then may we call and savely syng ♪
Victoria, yeve thankes for owre hom! ♪

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Vina, I can't believe it—the graffiti on the gym walls is still there! Look at this one—Morgan painted it after dreaming of being a famous artist.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Oh, right! Look at this photo—the sign on the movie theater has been nailed back up. And look, there are two dumb-looking fowlbeasts perched on top of it, haha.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Norport is in much better shape than the last time we saw it.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: I can't wait to go back and see it with my own eyes.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Uh-huh...

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: So, where did these photos come from?

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: The envelope only had the photos, no signature. But plenty of people have joined the engineering team to help rebuild our home. Some of them are old friends from Norport.

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Oh, there are two videotapes in here too. They're just some old, worn-out movies, but hey, Delphine, you love watching bad movies, don't you?

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Here you go.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Thank you.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Vina... are you okay? You seem a bit distracted.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Are you all going back?

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Why the serious look? We're just heading home early to do some housekeeping.

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Morgan, you were more excited than anyone when we said we were going home... or am I missing something?

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: How about you, Dagda?

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: I'll go lend them a hand. There's not much I can help with here, Vina.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: The Knights of the Tower Museum is coming along smoothly. My wish has been fulfilled.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Alright.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Vina, actually, we could still—
The bell tolls.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: It's 4:00. Vina...

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: I know... We can set out now.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Do you want to go see Diane?

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: No, I have a meeting with Parliament and the dukes.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Oh...

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Vina, those protesters outside—

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: I'll handle them personally. I know their concerns go beyond just Diane—they've been waiting a long time for a king.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Ha, well, that's definitely something the Glasgow Gang can't meddle in.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Morgan...

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Alright, alright. We'll head back and tidy up. You know, Norport is better than I expected—but not by much.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: We'll be waiting for you, Vina.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Vina, you could ask them to stay.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Of course, I'd love for the Glasgow Gang to stay together, but Auchterigg isn't their home.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Besides, just take a listen—there are plenty of people outside waiting for my response. But before I address them, I intend to bring back more than just empty promises from the dukes.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Vina, Parliament has done more than just make empty promises. They've helped revive our industries, restore order, resettle those affected by the war—

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Tell me, Delphine—does everyone now have an equal right to a decent life?

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: I need to show them that even without a king, we can prove this nation's potential to any doubters.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Let's go. I don't want to be late for the meeting with the dukes.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: We should sing something.

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Sing what?

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Any song will do, as long as it's not that blasted Auchterigg Carol.

spans.text: Any song will do, as long as it's not that blasted

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: Like the song Hannah hums every time she steps out of the ring? 'Hannah's a star, knocking 'em down, one by one, round after round♪'?

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Stuff it! I don't do that anymore!

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Besides, didn't you all say the song I made up to cheer for Vina was better?

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Oh, please. If I remember, you just replaced all the names in Dagda's favorite song with Vina, right?

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: I wonder if Vina even remembers something that silly.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Of course she does!

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: I know she mustn't have forgotten. It's just...

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Forget it. She said it best herself: looking forward is what really matters.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: And there's still a long road ahead, isn't there?

a.text: That day, we didn't take a detour to watch Diane's end, and we didn't listen to any radio broadcasts.

spans.text: That day, we didn't take a detour to watch Diane's end, and we didn't listen to any radio broadcasts.

a.text: I heard her Oripathy was so bad that they had to separate her to prevent any incidents… To think that her last shred of dignity came from Oripathy.

spans.text: I heard her Oripathy was so bad that they had to separate her to prevent any incidents… To think that her last shred of dignity came from Oripathy.

a.text: I've stopped trying to make sense of these things. As we left Central Londinium and caught sight of the factories of Norport…

spans.text: I've stopped trying to make sense of these things. As we left Central Londinium and caught sight of the factories of Norport…

steps.name: The Young Duke
steps.text: Vina, are you not attending the execution? They are relying on you to calm the many protesters there should things take an unfortunate turn.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: My good Earl of March, I'm not that indispensable. Besides, the Defense Forces are already maintaining order on-site, and several MPs are there to oversee the proceedings. They don't need me.

steps.name: The Young Duke
steps.text: Diane Weber truly was a hero. Shame really. She didn't really do anything wrong.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: Alexandrina, you've managed this matter well, but you need to be more heavy-handed.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: You're too concerned with dissenting voices, most of which don't matter.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: Madam Speaker, why not let us shield you from the storm until Londinium's Parliament fully matures?

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: Wellington's stance remains ambiguous, the Windermere demesne is simmering with unrest, and the Duke of Ashworth continues to keep a low profile as always.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: If the Speaker requires assistance, we wouldn't dare refuse. We must secure Victoria's future!

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Very well, since you've offered, I won't hesitate to accept.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Your Graces, you are undoubtedly aware of the dire situation with the Infected within the city. I must insist that you promptly reopen the supply route you have kept closed for over a month under the guise of ensuring safety.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Return the medicine and supplies we've already paid for. Of course, if you're still concerned, the Defense Forces can escort the shipment and clear out those 'bandits' along the way.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: Of course, those are minor issues. Now, how about my proposal for forming and training Infected fighting squads?

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: I understand you're considering forming Infected units in your own territory and want us to test its feasibility. That's fine, but I insist that the safety of the soldiers remain a priority.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: I'll make all the data available to you, of course, and to every other duke. After all, this has critical implications for the future strength of Victoria, doesn't it?

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: This is no simple matter, Madam Speaker. In truth, it has given me quite a headache. I'll be waiting eagerly for some good news from you.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: As for Your Grace, Duke of Caster, the Trilby Ashers should soon be delivering an invitation.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: After all these years, Londinium will finally reopen diplomatic channels with foreign envoys—this time in the name of Victoria. I trust you all will be in attendance when the time comes.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: But you'd best pray that Londinium presents herself in a form you can be proud of.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: I'll consider this a provocation, Alexandrina.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: From the moment you deliberately blocked Londinium from contacting other nations after the war, you've been provoking Parliament.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: You call it 'protection'. Where I'm from, we have another word for it—'kidnapping'.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Unfortunately for you, we always have our ways of reaching those whom we want.

steps.name: The Young Duke
steps.text: Oh, Vina, is it my turn to negotiate now?

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: No, Earl of March. We have nothing to discuss, and certainly no need to be friends.

steps.name: The Young Duke
steps.text: I'm afraid that's not for you to decide.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Hmph. Whatever your intentions may be, Londinium's affairs are none of Columbia's business.

steps.name: The Young Duke
steps.text: It seems you've found what you need to refuse any deals with me?

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: All I have is a few photos. Surely, you're aware of what's hidden beneath Londinium, right?

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: Oh?

steps.name: The Young Duke
steps.text: Vina, it seems you've managed to find yourself some leverage.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: Alexandrina, I admire your candor. But I must remind you, you're the Speaker of Parliament now, not just some... street thug with the Glasgow Gang.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Well, do you know how we used to keep corrupt cops away back in Norport?

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Either everyone pretends nothing happened and keeps things as they are, or we expose all their dirty laundry and everyone goes down in flames. It worked every time.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: And I'm sure your Graces understand that it has always been Victoria who has kept you safe, not the other way around. I believe your Grace has even said something of a similar nature before.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: Alexandrina... I'm starting to doubt our decision of choosing you as Speaker.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: You're mistaken. The decision was mine all along, not yours.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: I know your schedules are packed, so let's not digress anymore.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: I have a long list of things to discuss with you, Parliament seats, medical purchases, military reform, private communication lines...

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Supply routes, aid for reconstruction… so let's not waste time. Of course, you're free to continue arguing with me.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Don't worry, this time my sword won't be on your necks.

steps.name: Agitated Citizen
steps.text: She's coming! Everyone, get over here!

steps.name: Agitated Citizen
steps.text: If we can make the Speaker hear us, we can save that poor soldier's life.
On the street, the eagerly awaiting crowd surrounds Vina, who stands alone.
She knows they are all waiting for her answer.

steps.name: Agitated Citizen
steps.text: You've heard us! That innocent hero doesn't deserve this fate! It's not too late to change your mind!

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Sorry, I have nothing to say with regard to Diane.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: The Parliament has decided. As its Speaker, I stand by its decision.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Everyone, please disperse. Then again, if you absolutely insist on a resolution, you're welcome to stay.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Just now, I reclaimed many things from the visiting dukes—things that rightfully belonged to us and are crucial to our future.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: I will tell you about each of these things, one by one. This is the only matter I'll be addressing.
The sounds of protest begin to subside. While most await the outcome of the meeting, a few discontented voices still rise from the crowd.

steps.name: Agitated Citizen
steps.text: Is there really nothing that can be done for that poor soul? But why?

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: This isn't something that needs explaining. Do you want the Speaker to go back on her word?

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: If we start bending the rules now, the new laws passed by Parliament won't be worth the paper they're printed on.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Catherine, what brings you here?

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: Some old friends passing by saw the protest and worried things might get out of hand, so they asked me to see if I could help.

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: As luck would have it, quite a few workers just got off their shifts, heard about it, and came to support you.

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: Take a look.
As more and more workers gather around, they wave at Vina and spot familiar friends and family members among the protesters.
Conversations begin to ripple through the crowd, and the street suddenly comes alive with activity.

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: Looks like we're a bit late.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Lieutenant?! Aren't you supposed to be waiting at the Sanatorium for your departure?

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: Delphine told me about your situation. I wasn't planning to come, but once the others at the Sanatorium found out, they insisted on coming to see who was causing you trouble this time.

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: I couldn't stop them, so here we are.
A column of soldiers, marching in perfect formation and singing, approaches the congested crowd.
The noise instantly dies down as people instinctively make way for the soldiers, who march up to stand in front of Vina, forming a barrier between her and the protesters.

steps.name: Panting Soldier
steps.text: Vina, we all know you went to negotiate with the dukes today, to fight for us.

steps.name: Panting Soldier
steps.text: We're not about to let you be humiliated in front of the dukes today!

steps.name: Panting Soldier
steps.text: We might not be ready for another battle, but we'll win anyone in numbers!

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Thank you, all of you!

steps.name: Curious Child
steps.text: Everyone, come quick! I think they're over there!
A group of rowdy children fearlessly push through the crowd, squeezing their way right up to Vina.

steps.name: Curious Child
steps.text: It's really you!

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: You know me?

steps.name: Curious Child
steps.text: Of course! We've all heard your story. The great hero of the Exemplars, our very own Speaker!

steps.name: Curious Child
steps.text: I've made so many new friends recently—they're all people who walked back to Londinium with you.

steps.name: Curious Child
steps.text: They told me you would definitely recognize them. Take a look.

steps.name: Timid Child
steps.text: H-Hello, Vina?

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Annie? And there's Anabella! Oh, Jones! You're here too!

steps.name: Curious Child
steps.text: I guess they were telling the truth then!

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: But... Why have you come?

steps.name: Curious Child
steps.text: We ran into this lady with really tan skin. She said you might run into trouble and told us to come help you!

steps.name: Curious Child
steps.text: Uh... did we actually help?

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Of course you did!

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Thank you, Morgan.
More and more people gather in front of the steps, while those who had been protesting for Diane start to quiet down.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Sigh... whew—
She thinks about everything that has happened over the past few days.
She thinks about the drunken Diane, the departing Glasgow Gang, and the stolen crown.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Bloody hell...
Vina relaxes, sitting down on the steps and gazing at the fiery red sky.
The retired soldiers sit as well, huddling with the other citizens around Vina.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Ha, let's all take a break, okay?

steps.name: Curious Child
steps.text: Can I ask you something?

steps.name: Curious Child
steps.text: Will we ever have a king again?

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: I don't know, but not having a king might not be such a bad thing.

steps.name: Curious Child
steps.text: Why is that?

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: You'll understand when you grow up.

steps.name: Curious Child
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Uncertain Worker
steps.text: What do you think—will this be good or bad for Victoria?

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: It's still too early to tell.

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: If we have to accept the dawn of a new era, then we all need to change the way we think to keep up.

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: A Parliament regulated by the people, no more individual authority, no king… that's a first in Victorian history.

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: Even I have to admit, she may well be biting off more than she can chew.
Catherine glances at the Speaker, who is sitting on the steps without her expected grace, and can't help but wonder.
Vina is surrounded by the children. They all smile and laugh together.
Every so often, she raises her voice to share jokes about the dukes or what she managed to wrestle from the dukes. Things that belonged to the people.
The sunset's warm light bathes her figure, before slowly fading as the time passes.

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: I'd say the days ahead will only get better.
She breathes out a ring of smoke, watching as the thin wisps drift away into the dying light.

steps.name: Citywide Broadcast
steps.text: Parliament has passed a resolution: The crown will be placed on the throne in the Palace of Westhaleg, guarded around the clock by the Defense Forces.

steps.name: Citywide Broadcast
steps.text: Until a suitable candidate for the throne is identified, the Crown will be guarded by Parliament.

steps.name: Citywide Broadcast
steps.text: Once a candidate is chosen, a nationwide referendum will be conducted under Parliamentary review and supervision to finalize the coronation.

steps.name: Citywide Broadcast
steps.text: Additionally, Parliament will soon announce decisions regarding the distribution of living supplies and other public welfare matters—

steps.name: The Young Duke
steps.text: Ha, Parliamentary supervision.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: These meetings are truly exhausting. I much prefer settling matters at a grand banquet.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: At least there's wine when my lips are parched. *sigh* Sir Davis is certainly taking his sweet time fetching the wine.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: Your Grace, Duke of Caster, where are you headed next?

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: You already know the answer, so why pretend to ask?

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: Getting the news from you is quicker than waiting for Wellington's spies to report back.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: So how about you, Eleanor?

steps.name: The Young Duke
steps.text: Your Grace, we're hardly close enough to be exchanging warm farewells.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: Your words wound me, Eleanor. I suppose I'll have to present a fine bottle of wine on my next visit to old Normandy and ask him to put in a good word about me to you.

steps.name: The Young Duke
steps.text: Your carriage has arrived, sir. Allow me to get the door for you.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: Much obliged, Earl of March.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: And remember, we are all Victorians, after all.

steps.name: The Young Duke
steps.text: Of course.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: Ah, it's been so long since I last heard these bells. The sound brings back memories.

steps.name: Adulating Noble
steps.text: Your Grace, I've brought you one of the finest wines from our cellar!

steps.name: Adulating Noble
steps.text: Even those Sarkaz devils couldn't sniff this one out after they took my estate.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: Sir Davis, you are a man of rare wit.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: Rest assured, there will always be a place for you in the Gododdin territories.
The Duke of Gododdin takes a sip of the wine and turns to make a remark, but then suddenly freezes.
He is confronted with a stunning sight—

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: ...The sun has set...
The crimson sun sinks slowly, as though setting the entire city ablaze.
The scars the Sarkaz had torn into the city stand out even more vividly in the evening glow, as if they are still bleeding.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: (Sneezes) The winter sunset truly shows no mercy.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: Ah, much like the Speaker's attitude toward us, I suppose.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: I could send someone to deliver a few sets of winter clothing for Your Grace.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: Take care of yourself—Victoria isn't ready to do without you just yet.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: Many thanks.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: After all, we can't very well go before Wellington, can we?

steps.name: The Young Duke
steps.text: Why the sudden melancholy, Your Graces?

steps.name: The Young Duke
steps.text: I find this sunset rather breathtaking.

steps.name: The Young Duke
steps.text: Day fades into night, and night into day—how often do we get to witness such a sight?

steps.name: The Young Duke
steps.text: Londinium's thick fog and heavy clouds rarely part like this.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: Eleanor, back in the day, the lads at school would always joke that it was the sun that had to follow behind Londinium.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: It would rise as we please, and never set if we willed it.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: Now, though, she has to go full speed just to barely keep up with the setting sun.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: That thought keeps me awake at night.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: Day or night, sunrise or sunset, only Londinium can be Victoria's capital.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: Earl of March, remember my words.

steps.name: The Young Duke
steps.text: Droll. Very droll indeed.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: Hah, the sun really does move.
Another bell tolls.
More black-feathered fowlbeasts stir and take to the skies over the city, circling before flying through the steam towards the setting sun.
As the sun dips out of sight, the glow of the twin moons becomes ever clearer.
Night approaches.
